A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PieTa research. Text and rendered-page inspection support complete comparison of all nine pages, including Appendix A, equations, algorithms, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original WikiSQL experiments measuring sub-table selection and question-answering performance, including comparative results and ablations in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original WikiSQL experimental results and ablations in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same Llama3 output-layer fine-tuning, overlapping-window selection, iterative set-union combination, and stopping rule.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiSQL for training and evaluation of sub-table selection and table question answering. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains ITR, TabSQLify, and Holistic LM as comparators. Table 5 retains OmniTab without selection and with ITR or TabSQLify. Comparator membership is unchanged throughout.

E3.justification: Both retain 15,878 test examples, the reported five-epoch training on 56,355 instruction pairs, 3×3 windows, and the same exact-match, precision, and recall evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The original/union/gold-table comparison, table-size and answer-size analyses, qualitative examples, and Table 7 ablations of tuning, output format, and data balancing are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. Table 5 still reports 88.55% exact match for PieTa with OmniTab; Table 2 still reports 51.2% precision and 97.8% recall for PieTa iteration 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical task formulation, set-union construction, window-size counting expression, and algorithmic definitions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about capturing dependencies through iterative sub-table formation and improving WikiSQL selection and question-answering performance.

C2.justification: The union-versus-gold-table rationale, explanations of baseline and ablation outcomes, and limitation concerning independent optimization of selector and reader remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Model specifications, training settings, window sampling, prompt structure, and balanced-data construction remain identical, including Appendix A. The funding acknowledgment adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning, and all 20 cited works are unchanged. Reference text merely reflows across pages 8–9.

P1.justification: v3 inserts an Acknowledgments section naming Samsung Electronics and Korean government funding sources before Appendix A, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment shifts appendix text and Algorithm 2 downward and reflows references across pages 8–9. Figures, tables, captions, and graphical content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding attribution and causes limited appendix/reference reflow. The scientific exposition, methods, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, with no meaningful overall quality difference.
